program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion only checks whether a mug is right of the headphones, so it treats the clearly rightmost mug as complete even though the source mug remains on the left and the edit appears to add/move another mug while leaving a blurred mug-shaped remnant. Bind the check to the source mug’s identity and compare its position across source and edited images; distinguish actual progress toward the requested move from merely finding any mug on the right, and preserve the rubric’s partial/absent/unknown distinctions. The traces are consistently high-confidence and complete, so this is a criterion/binding failure, not a transport or dependency issue; do not simply force the reference label or lower confidence. The reference ‘partial’ constrains the aggregate, but does not establish which visual detail is ground truth—inspect whether the original mug has moved and whether the remnant indicates partial progress, rather than assuming the right-side mug satisfies the request.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The check invents source-image facts not present in the instruction: that the mug is blue, starts left of the headphones, and must be the same identifiable mug. It also adds a no-evidence-it-remains condition. These constraints narrow the requested outcome and can reject a valid edit; the saved binding and criteria therefore do not preserve the instruction.

The check adds an unsupported requirement that the source mug be relocated with no visible duplicate or remnant. The instruction only requires moving the mug to the right of the headphones; it does not rule out duplication or remnants. This invented constraint changes the fulfillment criteria.
